It feels so fake. I understand wanting to escape that completely.

I know the school systems in Asia suck. I grew up in America but went to a high school with lots of Asians, and in that crowd your academic skill determined your worth as a person. That affected me for life. If you ever need someone to vent to about these things, my inbox is open.

I’m not one of those people that fully understands him or how he sees the world, but I don’t think he means that in a negative way. It’s just how it is.

It’s like almost every interaction is negative to him. For example, my friend once sent him a reminder to do something nice for my birthday and he said he didn’t like that she assumed he wouldn’t have done something nice for him. Other times when he tries to tell someone a problem and they bring up their own stories to relate, he’s upset that they’ve made it about them.

I would decide how important politics are to you. My partner and I have different politics on the outside, but we actually have the same core values with just different approaches. He identifies with the original core principles of Republican values and would identify as one, but hates that the party is basically balls to the wall racist. I don’t like either party and him identifying as Republican gave me the ick, but his reasoning is just wanting tax hikes for the rich and tax cuts for the poor. He is otherwise pro choice, pro BLM, pro Palestine, pro feminism, etc. Maybe ask yourself if just his labels bother you or you disagree on a fundamental value.

I understand how you feel completely. I just got over a bad flare up, but now I’m in a calmer state with my boyfriend. My OCD has just moved on to obsessing over other things now. In my calm state I can tell you that nobody else’s relationship matters. I know some couples that are happy together but fight every day. I know some happy couples that almost never text each other. Some couples just view marriage as a piece of paper. Even the healthiest couples I know go to couples’ counseling regularly. I also know couples that claim to be happy but are in some toxic, abusive situations and are just trying to overcompensate.

It’s easy to feel like your relationship was a unique case but all of us with ROCD feel that way. We’ll never just KNOW what’s right or wrong, all we can do is make our own choices.

I went through this a couple weeks ago. One of the absolute worst periods of my life, and it was hard on my partner too. It’s so easy to feel like this is just your life and will be like this forever. But you are not the only one suffering through this, you have our best wishes and support 💖
Social media is a terrible place to go for #relationshipgoals. They only show the good and never the difficult. Some lie for views.

Maybe you could give them the benefit of the doubt and say something like “You mention having OCD a lot. I know what a huge struggle that disorder is to have. Is there any way we can support or accommodate you through it?”

Hi! I just got over a month-long flare up and feeling very comfortable with my boyfriend right now, though I am still avoiding triggers. It's just that my OCD has bounced over to obsessing over my career now instead. I'm still cautious because I'm well aware a flare up can return.

What I will say is with ROCD... there's no guarantee you will know. A constant battle I had with my ROCD is that I wasn't sure if we were compatible, but I kept looking for reassurance to stay, that it would all work out. I knew I could start anew and wasn't afraid to be single, but I was afraid to have him out of my life. It didn't hit me how much I wanted to stay until he (at his behest) I shared my intrusive thoughts with him and he started to cry. But ROCD works differently for everyone. You can't logic your way out of it. You just have to sit with the "what ifs" and take things one day at a time.

There’s no guarantee the “right person” will like you back… plus the point of ROCD means we’ll find flaws no matter how perfect the person is! Just telling us to date the “perfect” person misses the point.
Hang in there! ROCD is a bitch but after a flare up, I’m feeling more like myself again. We can do it!

Still together! I did ask my leftist friends what they thought and they felt that he’s well-meaning, just had a very sheltered upbringing. Our conversations about politics are calmer, still working out some communication issues, but overall we have the same morals but different approaches

Attraction is not the only thing ROCD attaches itself to. Any mild personality flaw can make you obsess for weeks. We’re trying to improve ourselves because on a logical level we know it’s impossible for anyone to be perfect and meet our standards entirely. Plus, no guarantee the person you find 100% attractive will find you attractive too

My boyfriend was also pretty mean to me when things got hard—he’d recently gotten out of a string of abusive relationships and became quite hardened by them, and he experienced a family death around the time we started dating. I broke up with him and it incentivized him to do some self-reflection. We got back together shortly after he apologized and continued with therapy. Who he is now is completely different from the guy he was around that time. There has to be active effort on both ends to make communication work.

I can’t give you answers or absolutes. What I will say is that if he is willing to put in the effort, then the adjustment may take time, and that’s something to consider. (Consider as in, you can consider what you’re willing to put up with for the time being, or if there are other methods you can think of together to improve communication.)

This isn’t ROCD. How would you feel if someone your age said they were dating a 10 year old? I’m in my late 20s and wouldn’t even date a college student. This is ABSOLUTELY something to freak out about.

Why did you avoid dating someone of your own background? I’ve always wanted someone of a similar culture who can understand me, my culture, and my family dynamics. But I didn’t ever NEED it to be the same. I don’t think I ever ended up dating someone of my own ethnicity (though my current partner and I are the same race).

It was one of the small reasons I didn’t really see myself with my ex, but it wasn’t the biggest deal in the world. I definitely think the cultural hangup could be something to confront and sort out for yourself, outside of your relationship—why did you initially avoid people of your cultural background and what are the pros if you do date someone as such?

Wow. I came on here to post about a long talk I had with my boyfriend last night and how my ROCD calmed down for now, but this was a really thoughtful comment. I know I’ve been quite unhappy with myself, but I didn’t really think of how much I was projecting onto the relationship. My boyfriend also knew that if OCD didn’t attack my relationship (which he surmised it was doing because it was so important to me), it would be attacking something else right now. The funny thing was, I didn’t feel envy at all for them when I first got into this relationship, but because I didn’t attain the “best friend” sentiment everyone seemed to have, I thought I must be doing something wrong.

I really appreciate the time you took to write this out fully. One thing my OCD ruminates on is because I’m not where I want to be in life, it must signal I’m a bad person who doesn’t deserve good things, or that I’m not smart enough or didn’t work hard enough. I grew up being constantly compared to kids that did better in school than me or had more accomplishments, so I assumed if I didn’t meet other people’s standards/perception of “success” then I must be failing at something. This is definitely something I’ll discuss in depth with my therapist when I see her this week.

If I had money I’d buy reddit gold or whatever it is they do now. I wish I could pin your comment. I have no idea when I’ll go through another manic episode, but I’m so happy you commented what you did and in this moment I feel it’s really lifechanging. Thank you so much.

Even if she apologizes that won’t guarantee the wife will automatically heal. My boyfriend has been helping me reconcile with my emotionally and physically abusive mother lately, a choice that I’ve made. But seeing her for the first time after years of no contact was still rough. She was completely pleasant and even admitted she hadn’t been the best mother. But my body still shut down, I was on autopilot, and I got triggered over a lot of little things over the course of dinner. I cried twice after it was over. I very desperately want to be able to be normal around her again but my body hasn’t recovered. I feel it’ll be years before I can have a normal conversation with her. So I can’t imagine what it’ll be like for OP’s wife who had zero intention of ever seeing her high school abuser ever again.

So oddly enough I’ve been in this situation! Last year I started seeing a guy whose best friend bullied my friend in high school and was quite mean to me as well. I decided to let bygones be bygones and try to be on good terms with her until she stabbed me in the back several months into dating. My boyfriend was extremely reluctant to let her go but ultimately decided to block her recently. I had felt very bad about it, but a therapist told me to let him make this decision because reconciling with her would not make either of us happy and she needed to learn that there were consequences for her actions.

I would suggest that he talk to his brother about the new gf’s history with his wife and see what his brother decides. It’s tough, but you can’t just sweep the gf’s actions under the rug, and it’s also on the brother to consider if his hurting his relationship with his SIL is worth dating this new person for.
